answer: Every agent identity stays costly to clone because it is bound to a scarce artifact that weathers on its own clock. First, registration mints each ID against a distinct marble token from a fixed quarry, so a sybil farm must acquire unique stock instead of copying keys. Second, each token accrues a glacier-slow umber patina: sequential maintenance proofs that cannot be parallelized, and transfer resets the clock. Cloning N identities costs N marbles plus N slow waits.
